summary_paragraph: A man with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, prior CABG, CVA, and chronic alcohol use was admitted after being found unconscious on the floor following heavy alcohol consumption. He reported sharp, reproducible left-sided chest pain and leg pain attributed to a fall. Evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal troponins and prior negative stress test; chest pain was deemed musculoskeletal. CT head and spine showed no acute abnormalities. Liver enzymes were elevated, consistent with acute alcoholic hepatitis, which improved with supportive care. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal but remained stable without symptoms. Electrolyte imbalances from dehydration resolved with IV fluids. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to reduce alcohol intake, continue cardiac and liver-protective medications, and follow up with primary care.
problems: Concussion with loss of consciousness of unspecified duration
